## Purpose and entry points
AnythingLLM is a self-hostable, multi-user AI workspace: users ingest documents, retrieve relevant context, chat with configurable LLMs, and run agents, flows, scheduled jobs, and integrations. It is a JavaScript/Node monorepo with three primary runtime processes: React UI (`frontend/src/main.jsx`, `frontend/src/App.jsx`), Express application/API (`server/index.js`), and document collector (`collector/index.js`). Docker is the principal packaged deployment (`docker/Dockerfile`, `docker/docker-compose.yml`).

## Client application and API boundary
The Vite/React SPA provides authentication, onboarding, workspace management, provider configuration, document management, and streaming chat UX. API-facing model modules isolate browser requests from UI components; the workspace-chat tree renders messages, citations, tool approvals, attachments, and agent output.
- `frontend/src/models/workspace.js`
- `frontend/src/components/WorkspaceChat/ChatContainer/index.jsx`
- `frontend/src/pages/WorkspaceSettings/index.jsx`

The browser is a client boundary: provider credentials, persistence, retrieval, authorization, and agent execution are server responsibilities.

## Core server and persistence
The Node/Express server owns REST/API endpoints, legacy/application endpoints, WebSocket agent interactions, authentication/authorization middleware, and boot-time initialization. Prisma defines the relational persistence contract for users, workspaces, chats, documents, memories, scheduled jobs, router rules, and configuration.
- `server/index.js`
- `server/endpoints/api/index.js`
- `server/prisma/schema.prisma`

Persistent local assets and uploaded/processed document storage live beneath `server/storage/`; deployments must preserve these volumes alongside the database and selected vector store.

## Document ingestion and retrieval pipeline
Uploads and connector-sourced content are sent to the separate collector service, which converts files, URLs, audio, and external-source payloads into normalized text/metadata. The application server’s document manager/splitter then chunks content, calls the configured embedding provider, and writes vectors through a selected vector database adapter. Workspace chat retrieves matching vectors as source context.
- `collector/processSingleFile/index.js`
- `collector/processLink/index.js`
- `server/utils/DocumentManager/index.js`
- `server/utils/EmbeddingWorkerManager.js`
- `server/utils/vectorDbProviders/base.js`

Collector integrations include repositories, Confluence, Drupal, Obsidian, Paperless-ngx, websites, and YouTube; audio handling includes Whisper-compatible providers and ffmpeg.

## Chat, models, and agent execution
Chat endpoints dispatch standard or OpenAI-compatible requests through provider adapters, optionally applying workspace context, memories, model-routing rules, and streaming. The provider abstraction supports local runtimes and external APIs, while embedding and vector-store adapters remain independently configurable.
- `server/endpoints/chat.js`
- `server/utils/chats/index.js`
- `server/utils/AiProviders/modelRouter/index.js`
- `server/utils/EmbeddingEngines/native/index.js`

Agent mode is a distinct orchestration path using the Aibitat engine, provider-specific tool calling, and plugins for web access, files, SQL, email/calendar, memory, MCP, and scheduled-job creation. Agent flows execute persisted no-code graphs with API-call, LLM-instruction, and web-scraping node executors.
- `server/utils/agents/aibitat/index.js`
- `server/utils/agents/aibitat/plugins/index.js`
- `server/utils/agentFlows/executor.js`

## Background automation and integrations
Background jobs embed documents, extract memories, synchronize watched documents, run scheduled prompts/agents, process Telegram chats, and clean generated artifacts. The server exposes OpenAI-compatible, embed-widget, browser-extension, mobile, Telegram, and web-push integration surfaces.
- `server/jobs/embedding-worker.js`
- `server/jobs/run-scheduled-job.js`
- `server/jobs/sync-watched-documents.js`
- `server/endpoints/api/openai/index.js`
- `server/endpoints/telegram.js`

External dependencies are deployment-selected: LLM/embedding/speech providers, vector databases (default LanceDB or remote alternatives), PostHog telemetry, model CDN downloads, and connector APIs.

## Deployment and adjacent Open Computer subsystem
Docker packages the multi-process application; cloud templates cover AWS, GCP, DigitalOcean, Kubernetes/Helm, and OpenShift. `open-computer/` is an adjacent agent-computer project, not part of the primary web/collector request path: its TypeScript CLI provisions or controls VMs, while its interface service brokers sessions, WebSockets, LLM proxying, browser/desktop control, and subagent orchestration.
- `cloud-deployments/helm/charts/anythingllm/templates/deployment.yaml`
- `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh`
- `open-computer/cli/src/index.ts`
- `open-computer/services/interface-service/index.js`
